title: The decoder from naturals back to first-order formulas inverts the numbering (OPEN in this ledger; the CONSTRUCTION is landed)
statement: FO.Formula.decode : Nat -> FO.Formula inverts the Goedel numbering: decode (code p) = p for every formula p. THE FUNCTION IS BUILT AND COMPUTES; THE THEOREM IS NOT PROVED. fo_decode.rs declares FO.Term.decodeAux, FO.Term.decode, FO.Formula.decodeAux and FO.Formula.decode (fuel-recursive, with a nine-way tag tree), and eleven module tests check the round trip AT CONCRETE CODES -- every FO.Term constructor and every FO.Formula constructor, by Kernel::def_eq. Those are instances, not a statement about all formulas. What is missing is the universally quantified theorem, and after building the decoder its cost is no longer an estimate: (1) size functions plus a fuel-additive round trip stated as 'forall t f, decodeAux (Nat.add f (size t)) (code t) = t' -- fuel on the LEFT of the add, so Nat.add f (Nat.succ x) iota-reduces and the recursive call lands on exactly the induction hypothesis's fuel, leaving only Nat.add_assoc and Nat.add_comm for the binary cases, with no Nat.le, no subtraction and no max; (2) one transport per tag, because FO.Code.fst (code (and_ p q)) is NOT definitionally 4 -- FO.Code.fst unfolds to Nat.Pair.fst (unpair ...) and unpair of a symbolic code is stuck, so each of the nine minors must rewrite along FO.Code.fst_pair and snd_pair before the tag tree iota-reduces; (3) size p <= code p, needed only to justify the self-fuelled wrapper decode n := decodeAux n n. Item (2) was invisible before the decoder existed.

formal.statement: theorem FO.Formula.decode_code : ((x0 : FO.Formula) -> Eq.{1} FO.Formula (FO.Formula.decode (FO.Formula.code x0)) x0)

provenance.source: this row records the measured remaining gap after lane arithmetization landed the numbering, its injectivity and the decoder CONSTRUCTION (W3-7, ADR-1640)

prior_art.what: arithmetization of syntax, in which decoding is done by primitive-recursive functions built from a pairing's projections
prior_art.where: Goedel, 'Ueber formal unentscheidbare Saetze der Principia Mathematica und verwandter Systeme I', Monatshefte fuer Mathematik und Physik 38 (1931)
prior_art.attribution: standard textbook attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source

notes:
THE STATEMENT IS AUTHORED, NOT EXTRACTED. FO.Formula.decode does not exist in the kernel, so the binder indices above are this lane's and not Kernel::render_lean's. It is written in the same style render_lean produces, which is what F:fo-completeness-henkin does for the same reason.

WHAT CHANGED WHEN THE DECODER WAS BUILT. Before fo_decode.rs, substCode could not be DEFINED, so its commuting lemma could not be STATED. It can now: FO.Code.substCode : Nat -> Nat -> Nat is declared (decode the formula code, decode the term code, substitute for de Bruijn index 0, re-encode) and is evaluation-tested, as is FO.Code.isFormulaCode : Nat -> Bool. So the remaining gap is purely a PROOF gap -- no construction is missing -- and the commuting lemma 'substCode (code p) (code t) = code (subst p (Subst.cons t Subst.id))' follows from the round trip in three Eq steps once the round trip exists.

WHAT REMAINS, SIZED AGAINST THE BUILT DECODER. (1) size functions for FO.Term and FO.Formula plus the fuel-additive round trip; the ADDITIVE form with the fuel on the LEFT is what removes the fuel-agreement lemma entirely, because the recursive call's fuel IS the induction hypothesis's fuel rather than merely bounded by it. (2) A transport along FO.Code.fst_pair / snd_pair in each of the 4 + 9 minors, to turn the stuck FO.Code.fst (code ...) into a literal numeral so the tag tree reduces. (3) size p <= code p for the self-fuelled wrapper only. None of it is research; all of it is proof-term engineering, and the module tests already pin every instance the theorem would generalize.

WHAT THE ARITHMETIZATION ALREADY BUYS THE HENKIN CONSTRUCTION. F:fo-completeness-henkin lists 'an enumeration of FO.Formula and a decidable equality on it' as one of its two obstructions. An injection FO.Formula -> Nat is the half of that which needs no Classical.em, and it is now proved; this row is the other half. The remaining obstruction there -- Lindenbaum's lemma needing excluded middle at every step -- is untouched by any of this and is a choice about what to prove, not work.
